# 一孔录 Yikonglu (English)

> Every line Yikonglu has read aloud can be checked here. Source text, page numbers in the base edition, the commentators' own words, pronunciation, our reading, and a public errata log, arranged book by book and chapter by chapter. Watch the videos on the platforms; come here to check.

## 论语 The Analects
- [1.1 Learning and practising it in season](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/1.html): What you learned, keep taking out to practise and to do. Today: watching the tutorial ten times is watching another bird fly.
- [1.2 Filial and fraternal duty as the root of ren](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/2.html): Filial and fraternal duty is where practising ren begins. Today: kind to strangers online, no patience for one's parents at home — that is starting from the far end.
- [1.3 Clever words and a pleasing face](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/3.html): Watch whether he does it to get the thing done, or only to be liked.
- [1.4 Three things I examine myself on daily](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/4.html): When you act for someone, did you hold anything back? Today: a colleague asks you to look over a plan; you can't be bothered to point out the flaw and say “looks good”.
- [1.5 Governing a state of a thousand chariots](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/5.html): Cheng Yi: “此言至浅……若推其极，尧舜之治亦不过此” — the words are plain, but pushed to the limit, even Yao and Shun governed no differently. Today: a shopkeeper who keeps his word, doesn't waste money, and doesn't send staff on private errands in the busy season.
- [1.6 A young man at home is filial](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/6.html): This is about order, not about choosing one and dropping the other. Today: the capable person who never studied has nothing to check himself against when he is wrong.
- [1.7 Honouring the worthy over good looks](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/7.html): Someone who never studied but does all this — Zixia says he has studied. Today: the elders who had only a few years of schooling.
- [1.8 A gentleman without weight has no dignity](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/8.html): Zhu Xi takes the words as they stand and does not talk his way around them. Today: the one person willing to tell you to your face tells you twice; if you don't change, the third time he says nothing.
- [1.9 Care at the end, remembrance of the distant](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/9.html): Put your heart into the places that are easy to neglect and easy to forget. Today: driving two hundred kilometres to stand ten minutes at a grave.
- [1.10 Whenever the Master arrives in a state](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/10.html): Coming to ask is not the same as handing you the job.
- [1.11 While the father lives, observe the son's intent](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/11.html): What is wrong, change now; what can wait, let wait — that is time given to what one cannot bear to let go. Today: the small factory a father left behind.
- [1.12 In the use of ritual, harmony is prized](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/12.html): Harmony alone, with nothing to regulate it, does not work either. Today: the team where everyone only ever says “looks good”.
- [1.13 Trust that comes close to what is right](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/13.html): The work happens before you say yes. Today: agreeing at midnight, without a thought, to lend the money.
- [1.14 A gentleman does not seek to eat his fill](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/14.html): Not going hungry on purpose; simply too occupied to mind.
- [1.15 Poor without flattery](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/15.html): Acknowledge what has been done, then push one step further. Today: from renting to owning without bowing or showing off — Confucius would say “that will do”.
- [1.16 Not troubled that others do not know me](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/xue-er/16.html): The book opens with “unrecognised and yet not resentful” and closes here; the two ends meet.
- [2.1 Governing by virtue](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/1.html): Not that decrees are unnecessary, but that the one who governs must first have gained something himself. Today: the form teacher whose word counts.
- [2.2 Thoughts without crookedness](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/2.html): The “without crookedness” lies in the reader, not entirely in the poems. Today: a novel about a villain can still bring a reader round.
- [2.3 Guiding them by decrees](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/3.html): Punishment and decree keep people from crime; virtue and ritual move them toward good. Today: the camera breaks, and the rubbish comes back.
- [2.4 At fifteen I set my heart on learning](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/4.html): Not a certificate issued automatically at a certain age, but a road of learning.
- [2.5 Meng Yizi asks about filial piety](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/5.html): Today: borrowing money to throw a lavish birthday banquet is “doing what one may not”.
- [2.6 Meng Wubo asks about filial piety](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/6.html): Three readings of one line, side by side. Today: staying up all night drinking, riding without a helmet.
- [2.7 Ziyou asks about filial piety](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/7.html): Both readings land on reverence. Today: sending money on time, but sounding impatient on the phone.
- [2.8 Zixia asks about filial piety (the hard part is the face)](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/8.html): All the work was done; the face never arrived.
- [2.9 Hui is not slow](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/9.html): Whether someone has learned shows outside the classroom.
- [2.10 Look at what he does](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/10.html): What he does, why he does it, whether he enjoys it. Today: leaving at six sharp the week the boss is away.
- [2.11 Reviewing the old to know the new](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/11.html): If you can only recite it, reheating it a hundred times still gives the same bowl.
- [2.12 The gentleman is not a vessel](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/12.html): Virtue made whole first, then it can be used anywhere — not learning a hundred trades. Today: the accountant everyone likes to ask for advice.
- [2.13 Act first, then speak](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/13.html): You still speak — only afterwards.
- [2.14 Inclusive, not partisan](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/14.html): Same dishes on the table, different reasons for the dinner.
- [2.15 Learning without thinking](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/15.html): One is empty, the other hangs in the air. Today: bookmarking online courses without thinking vs. building theories without reading.
- [2.16 Working at strange doctrines](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/16.html): Following Zhu Xi: burrowing into it is what does harm.
- [2.17 To know what you know](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/17.html): Admitting you do not know is where it starts.
- [2.18 Zizhang studies to gain office](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/18.html): Confucius promises nothing; he turns seeking office into a lesson in being a person.
- [2.19 Raise up the straight](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/19.html): The hard part is seeing who is straight. Today: promoting the people who only bring good news.
- [2.20 Approach them with dignity](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/20.html): Ji Kangzi asks for a method; Confucius answers with duty. Treating duty as a method goes wrong again.
- [2.21 Why do you not take part in government?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/21.html): The words are a pretext, and the point is also true.
- [2.22 A person without trustworthiness](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/22.html): Without it, the ox is an ox and the cart is a cart; they never connect.
- [2.23 Can ten generations be known?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/23.html): He watched two handovers and saw what stayed and what changed.
- [2.24 Sacrificing to spirits not one's own](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/wei-zheng/24.html): Taking gifts to the home of a boss you have nothing to do with; saying nothing in the meeting.
- [3.1 Eight rows of dancers in his courtyard](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/1.html): Four extra rows of dancers measure how hard a heart has become. Today: sitting in the boss's chair at the meeting.
- [3.2 The three families clear away to the Yong](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/2.html): They didn't even understand the song they sang. Today: a corner shop's banner “Welcoming heads of state”.
- [3.3 A person without humaneness — what of ritual?](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/3.html): Fill the eight rows, sing the emperor's ode — if the person is wrong, ritual and music can do nothing with him.
- [3.4 Lin Fang asks about the root of ritual](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/4.html): When both sides are off, lean towards the root. Today: a table full of dishes vs. a bowl of noodles.
- [3.5 The Yi and Di have rulers](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/5.html): The rebuke is aimed not at the Yi and Di but at his own people. Today: an old family firm where each branch keeps its own books.
- [3.6 The Ji sacrifice to Mount Tai](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/6.html): It was the Ji who needed saving, not Mount Tai. Today: working for a boss you cannot talk out of it.
- [3.7 The gentleman does not compete](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/7.html): The target does not lie; what is contested is whether your own hand is steady.
- [3.8 The painting comes after the white ground](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/8.html): If the ground is not smooth, every colour you put on comes out blotchy.
- [3.9 Not enough records](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/9.html): Confucius could tell it, but would not rest on his word alone. Today: grandmother's recipe — what's missing is the person standing at the stove.
- [3.10 The di sacrifice after the libation](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/10.html): Looking back, the records and the people are gone; looking around, the rite is there but the heart is not.
- [3.11 Someone asks about the di sacrifice](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/11.html): Saying “I don't know” does not mean he didn't know.
- [3.12 Sacrifice as if present](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/12.html): The form of the rite can be laid out by the book; the heart in it has to be brought by the one who sacrifices.
- [3.13 Better to court the stove](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/13.html): Do the thing right and everyone is easy to deal with; do it wrong and being on good terms with anyone won't help.
- [3.14 Zhou looked to the two dynasties](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/14.html): Following Zhou means following the work of improving on predecessors bit by bit. Today: the dishes at New Year's Eve dinner.
- [3.15 In the Grand Temple he asked about everything](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/15.html): Thirty years in, you still double-check.
- [3.16 In archery, piercing the hide is not the point](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/16.html): The contest is in what can be trained, not in what you were born with.
- [3.17 The sheep for announcing the new moon](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/17.html): The sheep marks the rite; keep the marker and the rite can still be recognised and restored. Today: an old shop that makes one pot of the old recipe at the winter solstice, not for sale.
- [3.18 Serving one's lord with full ritual](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/18.html): Not a bit extra — ritual simply requires this; Confucius says only “people take it for flattery”, with no insult back. Today: getting to the meeting early and filling in expense forms fully, and being mocked as a try-hard.
- [3.19 The lord employs his ministers with ritual](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/19.html): Each side looks only at its own end; Duke Ding was the ruler, and his question was answered with his own half. Today: a team lead first asks whether people are treated with enough respect; the team member first asks whether the work is done properly.
- [3.20 The Guanju: joy without excess](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/20.html): Not too little feeling, but feeling full without going over. Today: crying while reading your wedding vows, wiping your eyes and finishing the last line.
- [3.21 Duke Ai asks about the altar of the soil](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/21.html): The three “nots” are not “never mind” but a heavy rebuke, to make him careful in future. Today: forwarding an unverified message in a group chat — the recall button only works for two minutes.
- [3.22 Guan Zhong's capacity was small](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/22.html): Confucius does not say outright where the smallness lies; it shows in the luxury and usurpation. Today: the company grows, the boss's office becomes a palace, and the rules apply only to others.
- [3.23 The Master speaks of music to the Grand Music Master of Lu](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/23.html): First together, then harmonious, each part clear within the harmony, linked to the end. Today: a choir starts together, then blends, each voice part still audible, singing through in one breath.
- [3.24 The border warden of Yi asks to see him](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/24.html): A minor official saw Confucius's weight at first sight. Today: an old teacher moved off the podium runs free classes in the community, and more people come than were ever in his class.
- [3.25 The Shao is perfectly beautiful and perfectly good](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/25.html): The difference is in how it came: one was yielded, one was taken by force. Today: two equally splendid wins, one earned head-on, one after the opponent withdrew injured — the podium does not taste the same.
- [3.26 High position without generosity](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/ba-yi/26.html): It is not that it looks bad; there is nothing left to look at. Today: the man on the phone talking business at the door of the funeral hall — however large his gift, no one remembers he came.
- [4.1 Living among the humane is beautiful](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/1.html): Choose the wrong place to live and what you lose is not the house but the heart that tells right from wrong. Today: when buying a flat people ask about schools, the metro and sunlight, and rarely about how the neighbours treat one another.
- [4.2 The inhumane cannot long endure hardship](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/2.html): Long hardship makes people overstep, long pleasure makes them indulge; whether outside things can take a person away depends on whether the original heart is there. Today: someone out of work for six months still gets up at seven, shaves, and goes out for a run.
- [4.3 Only the humane can love and hate others](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/3.html): Everyone can like and dislike; the “can” lies in doing it rightly, which requires a heart that is not tied to anything. Today: a competition judge who sees a former student take the stage stands up, leaves the panel and gives no score for that round.
- [4.4 Set your heart on humaneness and there is no evil](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/4.html): Resolve does not guarantee no mistakes; it guarantees no intention to do wrong. Today: a learner driver scrapes the car three times in a year but never once runs a red light.
- [4.5 Wealth and rank are what people want](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/5.html): Do not take wealth that should not come, and do not dodge an undeserved poverty by crooked means; the big choices and the small daily work make each other. Today: the bus brakes hard, and the young man's first grab is to steady the old woman beside him.
- [4.6 I have not seen one who loves humaneness](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/6.html): Where the heart goes, the strength goes; the hard part is not strength but willingness. Today: the person with no time to exercise scrolls the phone for two hours before bed.
- [4.7 People's faults each follow their kind](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/7.html): Whether a fault leans too generous or too mean shows whether one is humane. Today: two people are half an hour late — one took a fallen old man to hospital, one overslept.
- [4.8 Hear the Way in the morning, die content at dusk](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/8.html): The hard part is not hearing, but still believing after one has heard. Life and death are the great matter; without something truly gained in the heart, no one can say “I may die at dusk.” Today: an old man in a hospital bed finally sees through what he never understood in a lifetime, takes his daughter's hand and says, “Now I am at peace.”
- [4.9 A scholar set on the Way who is ashamed of poor clothes](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/9.html): The mouth says the heart is set on the Way, but the heart is ordered about by things outside. The problem is not dressing poorly; it is treating poor dress as a shame. Today: someone who says he will devote himself to studying for the exam first spends three days picking the most expensive stationery.
- [4.10 No fixed yes, no fixed no; side with what is right](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/10.html): Do not decide in advance and do not refuse in advance; look only at whether it accords with what is right. “Nothing allowed, nothing forbidden” without rightness in charge is mere recklessness. Today: a line judge does not decide beforehand who should win, but bends down to see whether this one ball touched the line.
- [4.11 The gentleman cherishes virtue, the petty man his comfort](https://yikonglu.com/en/lunyu/li-ren/11.html): “Cherishing one's ground” is not homesickness; it is a heart that guards only its own little comfort. The whole difference between gentleman and petty man lies between public and private. Today: two people receive the same job offer in another city; one asks first what he can learn and whom he can help, the other only which place is more comfortable to stay in.
